title: Python SDK: Pydantic and Dataclass adapters + streaming response parsing helpers
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Customers building production apps want first-class typed parsing for model outputs and ergonomic streaming. Recent user feedback and internal SDK audits show inconsistent model-to-Python mappings, noisy post-processing for structured outputs, and poor ergonomics when consuming streaming tokens and partial structured payloads. Goal: Provide a small, backwards-compatible set of helpers in the Python SDK that make it straightforward to declare response schemas (pydantic models and dataclasses), parse synchronous and streaming outputs into those models, and surface validation/repair suggestions when outputs are malformed. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and migration docs for a Pydantic/Dataclass adapter layer and streaming parsing helpers for structured output and JSON-over-stream patterns.

Key constraints and decisions considered: 1) Backwards compatibility with current Response objects and existing user code paths must be preserved. 2) No heavy runtime dependencies: pydantic should be optional (soft dependency). If pydantic is missing we provide dataclass-first parsing with simple type checks. 3) Streaming parse must support partial JSON chunks, common malformed patterns from model outputs, and developer-friendly retry hooks. 4) API ergonomics should favor explicit parsing helpers (e.g., parse_response_as(MyModel)) over magic coercion.

Deliverables: a) new module redwood.sdk.response_adapters with parse_response_as, parse_stream_as helpers; b) PydanticAdapter and DataclassAdapter classes with a consistent interface; c) utilities for streaming JSON reassembly with lenient repair heuristics; d) migration guide and examples (notebooks and quickstart); e) unit + integration tests simulating both ideal and adversarial model outputs.
acceptance_criteria: parse_response_as(model, response) returns an instance of model for both pydantic.BaseModel and dataclasses without modifying original Response object
parse_stream_as(model, stream_iterator) yields model instances or partial models as streaming tokens arrive and handles partial JSON reassembly
When pydantic is not installed, users can still use dataclass adapters and get clear error messages explaining optional dependency
Repair heuristics handle common issues: trailing commas, unclosed braces, top-level text before JSON, and the adapter exposes a repair_summary with diagnostics
Comprehensive unit tests cover at least 95% of new module lines and CI runs integration tests against streaming harness
Docs and migration guide added to SDK docs with two runnable examples: notebook for sync parsing + demo for streaming parsing
Design reviewed and approved by SDK lead and one backend runtime engineer (review comments addressed)
tasks: Draft design doc and API surface and get sign-off from SDK lead (Marco Diaz)
Prototype PydanticAdapter and DataclassAdapter with minimal feature set
Implement parse_response_as for sync JSON outputs and add clear error types
Implement parse_stream_as that consumes async/sync iterators and reassembles JSON streams
Write lenient repair heuristics module and expose repair_summary in exceptions
Add unit tests for adapters and fuzzing tests for malformed model outputs
Add integration test using local runtime mock that streams token chunks
Update SDK changelog and migration guide in docs/python/structured-output.md
Create GH PR and address code review feedback
Prepare a short demo for next SDK sync (5-10 minute walkthrough)
notes: Design tradeoffs: We debated making pydantic a hard dependency versus optional. Decision: optional to keep install size low for users who only need basic dataclass parsing. Repair heuristics intentionally conservative to avoid hiding model degeneration. Streaming API will expose two modes: strict (raise on first malformed JSON) and lenient (attempt repairs and emit partial model with warnings).
